commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify missing data file test prerequisites
Keep the selected student in sync after re-sorting
commitResults.messageBody:
When an edit moves the selected student within a sorted view, such as
rescheduling a lesson in the upcoming list, the list highlights the
moved student while the details panel shows the student who took their
old row. The tutor can then read or act on the wrong student's details.

The edit replaces the student with a new object, and the sorted list
reports this as a removal and an addition at different rows. The
ListView selection model mishandles that move, so its selected index
and selected item no longer refer to the same student. The panel only
corrected the selection when the selected student disappeared, which
does not happen here.

Let's remember the selected student before the selection model sees
each change, find the same student in the updated list, and select that
row again. Selecting by row keeps the highlight and the details panel
in agreement. A renamed student is followed when the change replaces
only that student; otherwise the first student is selected, as before.

Fixes #154

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept common name characters and relationship markers
commitResults.messageBody:
Student and guardian names only accept ASCII letters, digits, and
spaces. Tutors cannot record names such as Jean-Luc Tan, Liam O'Brien,
or José Tan. A name such as Raj s/o Kumar is split at s/, so the
student is renamed to Raj and given the subject "o Kumar", while d/o
is rejected as an unsupported prefix.

Let's accept letters from any language, including accented letters and
combining marks, together with digits, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes,
full stops, and slashes. A name must still start with a letter or digit
so that blank or punctuation-only names stay invalid.

Let's also treat the whole-word relationship markers s/o, d/o, a/l, and
a/p as name text while tokenizing an n/ or gn/ value. Limiting this to
name values keeps s/ and a/ working as prefixes everywhere else.

Fixes #145

Student and guardian phone numbers have no maximum length, so clearly
invalid numbers such as a 50-digit number are accepted and saved.

Let's limit phone numbers to 15 digits, the longest number allowed by
the international numbering plan (ITU-T E.164). This keeps every real
local and international number valid while rejecting obvious typos.

Fixes #146

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn that clear also deletes archived students
commitResults.messageBody:
`clear` permanently deletes archived students as well as active ones,
without confirmation. The User Guide and Help only say that it clears
all records, so a tutor who archived former students to keep them can
lose them without warning.

and point to `archive` and `delete` as alternatives.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject control characters inside subject values
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide and `Subject` disallow control characters, but `add`,
`edit`, and `filter` collapse all whitespace in a subject before
validating it. A tab inside a subject is therefore converted to a space
and accepted instead of rejected.

Collapse only ordinary spaces in subjects, as learning focus and next
action already do, so that `Subject` validation rejects tabs and other
control characters. Remove the now unused helper in the filter parser
and clarify the rule in the User Guide.

The add, edit, archive, unarchive, and delete responses list every
field of the affected student, and help copies the whole command
reference into the result panel. The result panel is short, so users
must scroll a small scrollbar to read a confirmation that repeats what
the student card and Help window already show.

Let's name only the affected student in these responses and make help
confirm that the Help window opened. Schedule and unschedule responses
keep the lesson times, and error messages are unchanged, because users
need those details to confirm or correct a command.

Remove the now unused Messages#format and the help text constant, and
update the guides to describe the shorter feedback.

Fixes #122
Fixes #113

commitResults.messageTitle: Suggest plain keywords when a prefixed find fails
commitResults.messageBody:
Users who know the prefixes in add, edit, and filter may type
`find n/alex` or `find s/mathematics`. find treats these as literal
name text, so it reports `No students found.` with no hint, and users
may think the student does not exist.

Let's add a hint to the empty result when a keyword starts with a
command prefix, pointing to plain keywords and to filter. Such keywords
are still matched rather than rejected, because names may contain
markers such as s/o.

Fixes #148

commitResults.messageTitle: Add regression tests for query result views
commitResults.messageBody:
find and filter replace the archived view with an active one, so
commands such as archive work on their results. No test starts a
query from the archived view, so a change that keeps the archived
scope would go unnoticed.

Names may also contain accented letters, apostrophes, and markers such
as s/o, but name matching is tested only with plain ASCII names.

Add tests that run find and filter from the archived view, and test
name matching with accented letters, punctuation, and a keyword longer
than the matching part of a name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe active and archived scope in query Javadoc
commitResults.messageBody:
The FindCommand and ListCommand class comments say they list all
persons or students in the address book. Both commands show only one
result view scope, so the comments mislead readers about archived
students. Describe the scope each command actually lists.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep Active Students selected after find and filter
commitResults.messageBody:
find and filter clear the navigation highlight because the old All
Students label implied the full list. After the rename, their results
are still active students, and #106 expects Active Students to stay
highlighted after list, find, and filter.

Select Active Students after find and filter, as edit already does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the current query after editing a student
commitResults.messageBody:
A successful edit returns to the complete active list, so a tutor who
is updating several students in one find, filter, or upcoming result
must repeat the query before every edit.

Let's keep the current result view after an edit. A student who no
longer matches the query leaves the view, and the upcoming list
re-sorts after a name change. In both cases other students may move,
so edit adds the existing displayed-list notice, as schedule and
unschedule do. The navigation highlight stays on the current view.

Update the guides, the edit sequence diagram, and the manual tests to
describe the kept view.

Fixes #112

Master now reports unchanged edits with MESSAGE_NO_CHANGES and resets
the view for them. Keep the current view for unchanged edits as well,
so every edit leaves the result view in place, and keep the new User
Guide note about unchanged edits.

Master now keeps the current view after edit, warns about data files
that cannot be loaded, and documents the redesigned Help window. Keep
the edit list-update notice with the name-only message, keep the
data-load message test, and describe the shorter help feedback in the
refreshed User Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use student names in new archive test messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The archive and unarchive tests from master still build their expected
feedback with Messages#format, which this branch removes. Expect the
name-only feedback instead.
